From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: POC trial planning & workload intake - AcmeHealth

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the trial environment: 

1) Success criteria (primary):
- Inference latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 350ms for the primary route (clinical-notes-generation).
- Cost target: average token cost <= $0.0025/token equivalent for the evaluation window.
- Functional: model quality measured by AcmeHealth prompt set (NPS-style scoring) with >= 85% of sampled outputs meeting the guideline set.

2) Evaluation plan / timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize workload intake and mutual action plan (MAP).
- Week 1: Redwood provision POC environment (dedicated test pool) and ingest the workload profile.
- Week 2: Run 1-week evaluation against live-ish traffic (synthetic replay + small subset of real requests).
- Week 3: Joint review of latency/cost/quality and decision on expansion.

3) Ownership:
- Redwood: provisioning, performance tuning, quantization recommendations, runbook for test. (Ben lead, Dylan engineering support)
- AcmeHealth: provide representative prompt set and traffic profile, access to sample telemetry, product-owner signoff on success criteria. (Sam/Alex)

4) Workload intake (please confirm the numbers below or correct where needed):
- Typical sustained RPS: 6 requests/sec across region (US east).
- Typical prompt length (tokens): 80 tokens prompt / 220 tokens average response.
- Peak sustained concurrency: 8 concurrent model sessions.
- Burst patterns: hourly sync spike ~60 RPS for ~10-20s (end-of-hour batch for some clinics), daily morning peak 120 RPS for ~30s (every weekday 08:30-09:00).
- Max request size: up to 1,500 tokens total including context (we can cap in POC if needed).

Attachments: I attached a simple workload spreadsheet and a mutual action plan draft to make the intake concrete.

Next steps:
- Sam: confirm workload numbers (esp. burst patterns) and share the sample prompt set — target by Fri 3/19.
- Ben: will start provisioning once we get confirmation and the MAP signed.
- I'll schedule a 30m technical kickoff with Dylan and your infra lead.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0133

Marissa,

Thanks for the thorough recap — this looks right to me. Quick clarifications and a bit more detail on traffic profile from our engineering side: 

- Sustained RPS: 6/s is correct for production baseline on the clinical-notes route.
- Average token counts: prompts ~70-90 tokens; responses typically 180-260 tokens depending on verbosity.
- Concurrency: our frontend currently holds ~12 concurrent sessions during certain workflows; we expect to limit to 8 for the POC but will test up to 20.
- Burst behavior: there are two common bursts: (1) hour-boundary syncs from external systems (~55-80 RPS for 8-15s) and (2) morning batch startup 110-130 RPS for 20-40s across our multi-tenant pods. The numbers you put are conservative and fine to start.

I'll upload a sample of 500 prompt/response pairs (sanitized) to the Drive link you referenced by EOD Friday. Also attaching a short K6 script snippet that reproduces our peak morning burst if that helps.

Sam
Senior Product Manager, AcmeHealth

Hey team —

Appreciate the additional detail, Sam. A few practical notes from engineering and a proposed evaluation checklist so we can be aligned when the POC starts: 

Engineering notes / config suggestions:
- We'll provision a dedicated test pool with 4x A100-style GPUs (config subject to change after initial profiling).
- Default model variant: open Llama-based family (quantized FP16/INT8 path) unless you require a specific model. We'll include a fall-back to a larger variant if quality fails the prompt set.
- Autoscaling: config to be conservative for the trial (scale-out threshold 60% CPU/GPU-util) with burst capacity to handle 2x expected peak for short windows.

Proposed evaluation checklist (we'll measure these during Week 2 test window):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 per-route; confirm <350ms p95 for critical route.
- Cost: per-token cost and per-minute instance cost; compare against your cost target.
- Quality: run the shared 500-sample eval set and compute pass-rate vs your rubric (we'll supply evaluation harness).
- Resiliency: observe fallback behavior and queueing under burst; ensure graceful degradation (retries, throttling).

Next steps / timeline (updated):
- Tue 3/23: Redwood will validate the sample data and run a short profiler.
- Wed 3/24: Technical kickoff (30m) to confirm network access, API keys, and test schedule.
- Thu 3/25: Provision POC environment.
- Mon 3/29: Start 1-week evaluation window.

Sam — if you can confirm the Drive upload and drop the name of your infra contact, Dylan will loop them into the kickoff.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
